records.fact: Epoch AI estimates frontier AI training compute has grown about 5x/year since 2020.
records.caveat: Trend estimate; not a promise of future training runs or a direct capability scale.

records.fact: Epoch’s public trend page distinguishes estimated frontier training runs from all AI compute and reports methodological uncertainty.
records.caveat: Use a source’s model definition and confidence bounds before comparing to an inferred private run.

records.fact: GPT-5 with thinking used 50–80% fewer output tokens than o3 in OpenAI’s stated evaluations across several capability categories.
records.caveat: Output-token efficiency is not training-compute efficiency and comes from the model developer.

records.fact: OpenAI reports GPT-5 was trained on Microsoft Azure AI supercomputers.
records.caveat: The release does not disclose training FLOPs, data mixture, or a general solution to data constraints.

records.fact: OpenAI reported GPT-5 scored 74.9% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.0% on Aider Polyglot.
records.caveat: SWE-bench Verified uses a fixed 477-task subset; benchmark performance is not an employment-capability measure.

records.fact: OpenAI reported GPT-5 pro scored 88.4% on GPQA without tools and GPT-5 scored 94.6% on AIME 2025 without tools.
records.caveat: Narrow evaluations; GPQA/AIME do not measure sustained research autonomy.

records.fact: OpenAI reported GPT-5.4 achieved 75.0% on OSWorld-Verified versus a cited human 72.4% under that benchmark’s conditions.
records.caveat: The comparison is benchmark-specific, screenshot-based computer use; it is not general human equivalence.

records.fact: METR warns that measurements above 16 human-expert hours are unreliable with its current task suite.
records.caveat: Time horizons depend on task distribution, elicitation, and a 50%-success definition; do not extrapolate beyond displayed reliability.

records.fact: OpenAI introduced Operator in January 2025 and integrated it into ChatGPT agent in July 2025.
records.caveat: Product availability demonstrates an interface, not reliable autonomous completion of arbitrary work.

records.fact: OpenAI classified GPT-5-thinking as High capability in biological and chemical domains under its Preparedness Framework.
records.caveat: A developer’s safety classification is not a public demonstration of end-to-end harmful capability.

records.fact: Anthropic reported more than 80% of merged code was written by Claude in May 2026, within its own development context.
records.caveat: Internal metric; it does not establish causality, quality without review, or general R&D automation.

records.fact: Anthropic reports the typical engineer merged 8x as much code per day in Q2 2026 as in 2024.
records.unit: daily code merged per typical engineer, relative to 2024
records.caveat: LOC is an incomplete productivity metric; organization, tools, and task mix changed.

records.fact: OpenAI said it had secured more than 10 GW of compute capacity for the intelligence age.
records.caveat: Secured is not necessarily built, energized, operational, or dedicated to training.

records.fact: OpenAI’s House Select Committee update reports available compute of 0.2 GW in 2023, 0.6 GW in 2024, and about 1.9 GW in 2025.
records.caveat: Company-provided series; definition and utilization are not independently audited in the document.

records.fact: IEA estimated global data centres consumed 415 TWh in 2024, about 1.5% of global electricity, and projects about 945 TWh in 2030 in its Base Case.
records.caveat: All data-centre workloads, not only AI; 2030 is a scenario forecast.

records.fact: The IEA 2025 Base Case endpoints imply approximately 14.7% annual compound growth in data-centre electricity from 2024 to 2030.
records.caveat: Scenario estimate sensitive to AI uptake, efficiency, infrastructure, and local bottlenecks.

records.fact: IEA reported capital expenditure by five large technology companies exceeded $400bn in 2025 and was set to rise another 75% in 2026.
records.caveat: Company capex includes more than AI/data centres; 2026 is a forecast at publication.

records.fact: IEA reported data-centre electricity use grew 17% in 2025 while global electricity demand grew 3%.
records.caveat: Data-centre total, not a direct count of AI training energy.

records.fact: IEA characterizes a conventional data centre as about 10–25 MW, an AI-focused hyperscale facility as 100 MW or more, and its largest-planned example as 5,000 MW.
records.caveat: Illustrative facility classes/plans, not a count of operational facilities.

records.fact: Microsoft reported $41bn capital expenditures in FY2026 Q4; roughly two-thirds were short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs.
records.caveat: Company-wide capex includes AI and non-AI infrastructure; short-lived asset accounting is not a GPU count.

records.fact: Microsoft reported adding 31 data centers across five continents in FY2026 Q4, 88 during the fiscal year, and another GW of capacity in the quarter.
records.caveat: Company statement without a disclosed capacity-definition or AI-only breakdown.

records.fact: Alphabet’s Q2 2026 SEC exhibit reports $44.924bn in purchases of property and equipment, versus $22.446bn in Q2 2025.
records.unit: quarterly purchases of property and equipment
records.caveat: Company-wide property/equipment spending; does not isolate AI infrastructure.

records.fact: NVIDIA reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $96.221bn and Data Center revenue of $89.0bn, up 106% and 117% year over year respectively.
records.caveat: Vendor revenue is demand-side evidence, not an installed-GPU count or a measure of model capability.

records.fact: NVIDIA’s A100 80GB datasheet lists 80 GB HBM2e, 2,039 GB/s memory bandwidth, and 400 W maximum TDP for the NVLink model.
records.caveat: SKU/precision dependent peak specifications; not delivered training throughput.

records.fact: NVIDIA documentation lists H100 SXM at 80 GB HBM3 and H200 SXM at 141 GB HBM3e.
records.caveat: SXM values; other form factors and product revisions differ.

records.fact: NVIDIA documentation lists B200 SXM at 180 GB HBM3e and B300 SXM at 288 GB HBM3e.
records.caveat: Memory capacity alone does not determine cluster throughput or available supply.

records.fact: NVIDIA lists H200, B200, and B300 memory bandwidth at 4.80, up to 8, and up to 8 TB/s respectively.
records.caveat: Vendor peak bandwidth, with workload-dependent utilization.

records.fact: NVIDIA’s GB200 NVL72 contains 72 Blackwell GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in one liquid-cooled rack-scale system.
records.caveat: Product architecture, not an assertion of installed fleet count or delivered utilization.

records.fact: Anthropic’s July 2026 transparency update says its Responsible Scaling Policy was updated in February 2026 and its Frontier Compliance Framework was published in December 2025.
records.caveat: Published frameworks describe intent/process; they are not independent verification of implementation.

records.fact: Anthropic’s roadmap lists a September 30, 2026 target for security work and says an isolated-network prototype is being explored at small scale.
records.caveat: Target/prototype, not completed security assurance; the date is after this corpus cutoff by five days.

records.fact: Anthropic says its strongest models as of February 22, 2026 were protected with ASL-3 safeguards for specified high-consequence capability risks.
records.caveat: Company-defined safeguards for scoped risks; it does not resolve broader alignment or theft risk.

records.fact: Anthropic reported September 2026 evaluations found its models useful for some tactical intelligence-targeting and conventional-weapons tasks, and added on-platform classifiers.
records.caveat: Evaluation summary does not quantify operational effectiveness or show deployment outside safeguards.

records.fact: BIS announced the AI Diffusion Rule on January 13, 2025, covering advanced chips, certain closed model weights, and large advanced-compute clusters.
records.sourcePublisher: US Bureau of Industry and Security
records.caveat: Announcement text; later policy changes matter.

records.fact: BIS rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule in May 2025 before its planned May 15 compliance date and announced additional semiconductor-control actions.
records.sourcePublisher: US Bureau of Industry and Security
records.caveat: Rescission of that rule does not eliminate all pre-existing or subsequent controls.

records.fact: BIS’s December 2024 action added controls on high-bandwidth memory and listed 140 entities in connection with advanced semiconductor concerns.
records.sourcePublisher: US Bureau of Industry and Security
records.caveat: A legal/policy action; it neither measures compliance nor establishes strategic effects.

records.fact: BIS’s May 2025 counter-diversion guidance identifies 10 MW-or-larger data centers as meriting additional scrutiny in specified advanced-computing transactions.
records.sourcePublisher: US Bureau of Industry and Security
records.caveat: Guidance for transaction scrutiny; it is not a blanket capacity prohibition or a measured strategic outcome.

records.fact: Anthropic’s June 2026 Advanced AI Framework advocates rules for models trained with more than 10^25 FLOPs at companies above $500m AI revenue or $1bn AI R&D spend.
records.caveat: Company policy proposal, not enacted law.

records.fact: The IEA says data centres accounted for around half of US electricity-demand growth in 2025.
records.caveat: Energy-sector aggregate, not evidence of any particular procurement programme.

records.fact: An advanced Gemini Deep Think model solved five of six IMO 2025 problems for 35 of 42 points; IMO coordinators graded and certified the result under the student criteria.
records.caveat: Google reports the model setup; the external grading validates the submitted solutions, not broad research autonomy.

records.fact: OpenAI reported GPT-6 Astra scored 96.0% on GPQA Diamond and 59.3% on Agents’ Last Exam in its September 2026 release results.
records.caveat: The release places GPQA Diamond in its academic results and Agents’ Last Exam in computer-use results; scores and test setups are not a common intelligence scale.

records.fact: DeepSeek reports that its R1-Zero research variant developed reasoning capability through large-scale reinforcement learning without preliminary supervised fine-tuning.
records.caveat: This claim is specifically about R1-Zero, not every stage of DeepSeek-R1; a different learning signal does not make high-quality training data unlimited.

records.fact: A 2025 preprint demonstrated a 3.5-billion-parameter recurrent-depth model that iterates an internal block at test time and reported reasoning gains at a compute load equivalent to 50 billion parameters.
records.caveat: Proof-of-concept research architecture; it is not evidence that deployed frontier models use latent recurrent reasoning.

records.fact: AIDE², a September 2026 preprint, reports seven successive changes to an AI research agent’s own code during an autonomous eight-day run, with gains on four held-out benchmarks.
records.unit: accepted changes; run duration; held-out benchmarks
records.caveat: Very recent unreviewed result on agent software optimization, not an autonomous succession of newly trained frontier models.

records.fact: A 2026 preprint found monitors detected 60–94% of explicitly induced behavior shifts, while implicit influence reduced detection by 41–46 percentage points in two task settings.
records.caveat: Single preprint benchmark across four task formats; the two-setting result is not a general measurement of deployed oversight reliability.

records.fact: OpenAI states that GPT-6 Astra meets its Critical cybersecurity capability threshold and says its post-Hugging-Face hardening included isolation and network controls, expanded monitoring, and stricter training controls.
records.caveat: OpenAI’s own classification and account of safeguards; no public independent assessment establishes security against a top-tier state actor.

records.fact: The US Department of Energy launched the Genesis Mission Consortium, a public-private partnership involving DOE, National Laboratories, private-sector leaders, and academic institutions for AI-enabled scientific discovery.
records.caveat: A government research coalition, not evidence of the unified government-led AGI project forecast in the original essay.

records.fact: NVIDIA’s Rubin architecture post lists up to 288 GB HBM4 memory and up to 22 TB/s peak memory bandwidth per Rubin GPU.
records.unit: GB HBM4; TB/s peak memory bandwidth
records.caveat: Vendor-announced peak specifications, not measured application throughput or a count of deployed hardware.

records.fact: Epoch AI and EPRI forecast the largest individual frontier-model training runs in 2030 at 4–16 GW.
records.caveat: A modelled training-run range, not observed power or the total capacity of a company or campus.

records.fact: LBNL projects all US data centers will consume 11.8% of national electricity in 2030 in its reference case, with scenarios from 9.5% to 15.3%.
records.caveat: Includes non-AI workloads and models demand; does not directly forecast new generation or a single AI cluster.

records.fact: Stanford AI Index reports US private AI investment of $285.9bn in 2025 and Chinese private AI investment of $12.4bn.
records.caveat: Private funding undercounts state-led investment and is not a direct measure of model-training compute.

records.fact: Stanford AI Index says the top US model led the top Chinese model by 2.7% in its March 2026 performance comparison.
records.caveat: Benchmark aggregation and the reference date limit what this says about broad capability or strategic capacity.
